title: Chicken Parmesan for a Crowd
description:
When you prepare crisp, golden cutlets in advance and stockpile them in your freezer, you open up all kinds of
options for speedy dinners. The best part? They go from frozen to perfection in a mere 15 minutes.
ingredients: 4 cups Italian style panko (Japanese breadcrumbs), or plain panko with garlic salt, oregano, or Italian spice mix
8 boneless skinless chicken breasts (or 16 thin-sliced breasts or the 8 individual breasts cut in half horizontally)
2 cups homemade or store-bought tomato sauce
directions: Prepare cutlets: Preheat oven to 400 degrees. Toss panko, olive oil, and
1 teaspoon salt on a rimmed baking sheet. Bake, stirring twice, until
deep golden brown, about 15 minutes. Let cool completely. (Crush a
few handfuls, to help crumbs adhere.) Whisk eggs in a bowl. Pat dry
chicken cutlets; season with salt and pepper. Dredge in flour, tapping off
excess. Dip in eggs; coat with panko, patting to adhere. Lay cutlets in
layers on a baking sheet, with parchment in between each. Freeze 2
hours, then up to 1 month in resealable plastic bags.
Bake cutlets: Arrange on a wire rack set on a rimmed baking sheet. Bake
at 450 degrees, flipping once, until cooked through, about 10 to 12
minutes. (If cutlets are not frozen, bake about 8 to 10 minutes.)
Preheat broiler with rack 4 inches from heat source. Top each cutlet with basil leaves, sauce, a sprinkling
of parmesan, and mozzarella, dividing evenly. Broil until cheese is melted, 2 minutes. Top with a little
more Parmesan and more basil, if desired; serve.
